failures.title: Vauxhall EB2ADTS Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Wet timing belt degradation - pre-2022 EB2ADTS units
items.whatHappens: The EB2ADTS uses a timing belt that runs in an oil bath - a design intended to reduce friction and noise. However, fuel contamination in the engine oil (from incomplete combustion during cold starts and short journeys) causes the belt material to degrade prematurely. The belt sheds rubber fragments into the oil system, which blocks the oil pickup strainer and vacuum pump, leading to oil starvation and eventual engine seizure. Stellantis has issued extended warranty coverage for this issue, covering affected engines for 10 years or 175,000 km where service history is maintained .
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early - before the oil pressure warning light appears - a belt replacement and oil system flush (£600-£1,200) is sufficient. If the oil pickup has become blocked, camshaft and crankshaft scoring is highly likely, requiring a full replacement engine .

items.title: Excessive oil consumption - pre-2022 EB2ADTS
items.whatHappens: Reports of oil consumption up to 1 litre per 1,000-2,000 km are documented on 1.2 PureTech engines . The issue is linked to piston ring design and bore honing on earlier production units, allowing oil to pass into the combustion chamber. This leads to spark plug fouling, catalytic converter damage, and the engine management light appearing.
items.repairVsReplace: Addressing oil consumption requires a bottom-end rebuild with replacement piston rings - a labour-intensive job typically costing £1,500-£3,000. On older, lower-value hosts, this cost often makes a replacement engine the more economical choice.

items.title: Turbocharger clogging and carbon buildup
items.whatHappens: The small turbocharger on the EB2ADTS is susceptible to carbon buildup from EGR gases and oil vapour, particularly in vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys. Blocked turbo vanes cause reduced power, increased fuel consumption, and eventually turbocharger failure.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo cleaning (de-coking) costs £300-£600 and can restore performance on units caught early. Full turbo replacement runs £800-£1,500.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2022 EB2ADTS units received a revised timing chain design (replacing the wet belt), addressing the most catastrophic failure mode . These later engines are considered significantly more reliable. Units built from late 2022 onwards carry the EB2ADTS code but feature the chain-drive design. Additionally, Stellantis recommends reducing belt replacement intervals to 60,000 miles on earlier engines to mitigate failure risk .

variants.title: EB2ADTS Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: The EB2ADTS is one of several 1.2-litre PureTech variants. The key distinction is between the earlier EB2DT/EB2DTS units (pre-2017, wet belt) and the EB2ADTS (2017 onwards), which represents a technical revision. Post-2022 EB2ADTS units received a further significant change: the replacement of the wet belt with a timing chain . - Fitted to: Vauxhall Corsa F, Grandland X, Crossland X, Mokka; Peugeot 208 II, 2008 II, 308 II, 3008 II; Citroën C3 III, C4 III, C5 Aircross; DS 3 Crossback, DS 7 Crossback - Key technical difference: This is the revised 1.2 turbo engine with improved belt materials and revised ECU calibration, producing 96 kW (130 hp) and 230 Nm torque . Still uses the wet timing belt design, but with improved durability over the earlier EB2DT. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the wet belt degradation pattern with earlier EB2DT/EB2DTS engines. Stellantis extended warranty coverage applies to this variant for vehicles manufactured up to June 2022 . - Interchange note: The EB2ADTS engine code is not a straight swap with EB2DT. The ECU calibration, fuel injectors, and emissions equipment differ. Always confirm the exact sub-code before purchasing a replacement. - Fitted to: Vauxhall Corsa F, Grandland X, Mokka (late 2022 production onwards); Peugeot 208 II, 2008 II; Citroën C3 III, C4 III - Key technical difference: The wet timing belt has been replaced with a timing chain in this revision . This fundamentally addresses the belt-degradation failure mode. The engine also received updated piston rings to address oil consumption. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Post-2022 chain-drive units are significantly more reliable than the wet-belt generation. No major failure patterns are yet documented for these later units . - Interchange note: Not a straightforward swap with earlier EB2ADTS units. The cylinder head, timing cover, and engine management system differ. Always verify compatibility using the engine code stamped on the block. - Fitted to: Vauxhall Corsa F Hybrid, Peugeot 208 Hybrid, Citroën C3 Hybrid, DS 3 Hybrid - Key technical difference: Same 96 kW power output but combined with a 48V mild-hybrid system and a belt-integrated starter-generator (BiSG). Additional cooling and electrical components are fitted. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the post-2022 chain-drive design. No unique failure patterns beyond the standard EB2ADTS mechanical issues. - Interchange note: Not interchangeable with standard EB2ADTS. The hybrid-specific wiring harness, cooling system, and ECU are completely different.

relatives.description: the previous-generation 1.2-litre PureTech engine (110-130 hp, 2012-2018) used the same wet belt design but with earlier belt materials that degraded faster. Owners with EB2DT units should note that the EB2ADTS received improved belt compounds, though the fundamental wet belt design remained until 2022.

introduced in late 2022, this variant finally replaces the wet belt with a timing chain. If you're replacing a failed EB2ADTS, consider whether a chain-drive unit is available and compatible with your vehicle's engine bay and management system.

The Peugeot EB2ADTS is the identical mechanical unit to the Vauxhall EB2ADTS - same assembly line, same wet belt design, same failures. The engine code may appear as EB2ADTS on both brands, with only minor ECU calibration differences for the respective marques. See our for identical cross-brand fitment data. The Citroën EB2ADTS and DS EB2ADTS are also the same engine.

variants.closing: The EB2ADTS engine code is stamped on a metal plate on the cylinder block (visible from the front, under the intake manifold). It also appears on your V5C registration document in the Engine Number field - the first characters will show EB2ADTS (or HN05 for the factory designation). If you're unsure, enter your registration above and we'll confirm your exact fitment using the Vauxhall/Stellantis database.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement EB2ADTS - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used EB2ADTS makes sense only where the timing belt replacement has already been documented and the unit has clear service history. Given the wet belt issues on pre-2022 engines, buying a used unit without belt history is a gamble - the oil pickup could already be partially blocked. For lower-value Corsa F or Crossland X examples where replacement cost exceeds vehicle value, a used unit with proven belt history (£500-£1,200) may be the only financially viable option.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper EB2ADTS recon from a Stellantis-specialist workshop addresses the wet belt (replaced with the updated belt material or chain conversion on later-design engines), oil pump and pickup cleaning, piston rings (to address oil consumption), and a full turbo inspection. For most owners, this is the right call - the engine comes with a warranty and the known failure points are addressed at the source.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified where the original engine has suffered oil starvation damage but the cylinder head and block are salvageable. This is the highest-cost option but allows for upgraded components (revised piston rings, chain conversion on earlier engines) to be fitted. For high-mileage vehicles where the owner plans to keep the car long-term, a rebuilt unit offers the best longevity.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All our vetted UK Stellantis specialists offer supply-only, supply-and-fit, and nationwide delivery options. Every reconditioned and rebuilt EB2ADTS comes with a minimum 12-month warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The EB2ADTS appears in Corsa F and Crossland X vehicles that can be worth as little as £4,000-£8,000 on the used market. With reconditioned supply costs starting at £1,600, a fitted replacement at £2,200 represents 30-55% of vehicle value. For lower-value examples (sub-£5,000 Corsa F models), a used unit with documented belt history may be the more financially prudent choice. However, for Grandland X and Mokka examples with £10,000+ retained values, a reconditioned unit is comfortably justified.
